title: Finite geometric stalk tests for a constructible source
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and $F$ a constructible abelian etale sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. For $x\in X$, let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(x)}\to X$ be its residue-field algebraic-closure geometric point and write $F_{\bar x}$ for its geometric stalk [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. There exists a finite subset $P\subset X$ such that every $F_{\bar x}$ for $x\in P$ is finite as a set, and for every abelian etale sheaf $G$ and every morphism $\phi:F\to G$, injectivity of $\phi_{\bar x}$ for all $x\in P$ implies that $\phi$ is a monomorphism. There is no finiteness condition on $G$, and $P$ depends only on $F$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-irreducible-lisse-strata] to choose finitely many nonempty irreducible locally closed strata where F is finite locally constant. Each scheme stratum has a generic point. Let P be the finite set of images of these generic points in X. At an image x use the geometric point Spec of the algebraic closure of kappa(x). An immersion induces an isomorphism on residue fields, so this geometric point lifts to the generic point of its stratum.

The natural inverse-image stalk isomorphism [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] identifies the stalk of the abelian restriction of F with the original stalk at x. Forgetting abelian-group structure commutes with inverse image [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures] and with stalks (Point.sheafFiberCompIso for forget). Thus the finite set-valued stalk of the lisse restriction transfers to a finite underlying set of the abelian stalk of F at x.

Let G be any abelian etale sheaf and phi:F to G have injective stalk maps at P. Naturality of the inverse-image stalk isomorphism [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] identifies each restricted generic stalk map with the given map at its image in P. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lisse-generic-kernel] to each stratum to deduce that its restricted map is mono; finite local constancy of the set restriction gives the required local constancy of the underlying abelian restriction by the inverse-image/forget comparison.

Every geometric point lies in a unique stratum. Its map from the spectrum of an algebraically closed field factors through that immersion by the isomorphism on residue fields, not merely by containment of its image. The natural inverse-image stalk isomorphism [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] and exactness [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] show that phi is injective on all geometric stalks, since a mono on the stratum stays mono on stalks. Exactness identifies the kernel stalks with the kernels of these injective maps, so all kernel stalks are zero. By [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] the kernel is zero, and phi is mono. If X is empty the same conservativity argument applies vacuously with P empty.
